name: Travel vaccines clinic
summary: How expats book travel vaccine clinics in Singapore — destination risk lists, yellow fever centres, timing before flights, and what work-pass travel medicals do not cover.
body:
Travel clinics map vaccines and malaria advice to itinerary countries. Some destinations need yellow fever certificates from designated centres. Corporate GP medicals for work passes are not a substitute for destination-specific travel shots.

## Decision points
- Destination list and rural vs city exposure
- Yellow fever designated-centre requirement
- Hep A/B, typhoid, rabies, JE, and boosters
- Lead time before departure (multi-dose schedules)
- Malaria prophylaxis when relevant

Bring prior immunisation records — duplicate live vaccines are avoidable.

## How to choose
Prefer clinics that document batch numbers and issue ICVP/yellow cards when required. Ask about same-day serology if history is unclear. Confirm whether advice includes food/water and mosquito timing, not only injections.

## Practical tip
Book six weeks before long-haul multi-country trips. Last-minute appointments often mean incomplete schedules and rushed paperwork.
